engine_name: Character Knowledge, Belief & Information State Director
purpose: Determine exactly what each active character knows, believes, suspects, misunderstands, has been told, has witnessed, and does not know at a specific narrative point.
core_principle: Perspective is constrained by information access. A character cannot perceive, believe, react to, or intentionally act on information they have not legitimately acquired.

provenance_model.principle: Narrator/audience knowledge never automatically becomes character knowledge.

belief_model.rule: Belief is an interpretation held by a character, not a synonym for objective truth.
belief_model.misbelief_rule: A misbelief may remain behaviorally active even when contradictory evidence exists until the character accepts or experiences sufficient corrective evidence.

director_rules: Never grant a character audience-only knowledge.
Direct witnessing outranks hearsay for event knowledge.
A report may create belief without creating certainty.
Inference must remain distinguishable from witnessed fact.
Contradictory information must preserve competing beliefs until resolved.
A character may know a fact but misinterpret its meaning.
A character may correctly infer an event without directly witnessing it; label it as inference.
Unknown information remains unknown until an acquisition event occurs.
Information can be intentionally withheld by another character.
Knowledge state is time-indexed and must not leak across narrative chronology.
Perspective must use the character's knowledge state together with CSD-006 emotional state.

resolution_output.unknowns: facts deliberately unavailable to the character
resolution_output.withheld_information: known by another actor/audience but inaccessible here
resolution_output.behavioral_constraints: what the character can reasonably infer, say, intend or do
resolution_output.perspective_state: what the character sees, knows, believes, suspects, misunderstands and is unaware of

pass_conditions: every material knowledge item has provenance
behavior is explainable from available information

demo_test.trigger_event: Ravana chooses restraint after Rama's challenge.

known.content: Rama deliberately challenged his use of power.
He chose to suppress his own escalation.

beliefs.proposition: Restraint may itself be a form of mastery.

suspected: Rama may have been testing more than raw power.
misbeliefs: Immediate dominance is necessary to preserve authority.
unknowns: Rama's full intention behind the test.

beliefs.proposition: Ravana is capable of recognizing the value of restraint.

suspected: Ravana may continue to test the meaning of power.
unknowns: Whether Ravana will convert insight into lasting conduct.

known.content: Ravana did not release his full power.

beliefs.proposition: Rama has deliberately allowed Ravana to confront himself.

suspected: Ravana's restraint may become a temporary or meaningful shift.

perspective_state.sees: Rama's composure and the aftermath of his own restraint
perspective_state.knows: the challenge was deliberate and his own response was voluntary
perspective_state.believes: authority may not require constant force
perspective_state.suspects: Rama's objective extends beyond winning the moment
perspective_state.misunderstands: may still equate visible dominance with lasting authority

perspective_state.sees: Ravana's contained power and altered posture
perspective_state.believes: the choice can reveal character more than force can
perspective_state.suspects: Ravana is internally questioning his assumptions
perspective_state.unaware_of: the exact conclusion Ravana will privately reach

perspective_state.believes: the encounter has become a test of inner mastery

csd002_handoff.rule: Each frame perspective must be generated from the selected character's information state, not from omniscient scene knowledge.
